newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani rice prices seen firming.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani rice prices seen firming.

text.p: Pakistani rice export prices were expected to firm on increased demand from abroad, particularly Iraq, dealers said on Thursday.
"Export prices went up after domestic prices rose on news that Iraq wants to buy a substantial quantity of rice in 1997," Khalid Ghori of Matco Rice Processing said.
Ghori said Iraq was still exploring rice markets following its oil-for-food deal with the United Nations.
He said the state-run Rice Export Corporation had invited tenders by December 24 for the sale and export of 40,000/45,000 tonnes IRRI-6 rice. "The auction may attract Iraqi importers."
In the domestic markets, prices had not fluctuated much as big farmers were holding the crop on expectations of higher prices following Iraq's entry into the market, he said.
Rice exports rose 58.96 percent to 116,980 tonnes worth $35 million in November from 73,593 worth $25 million in October.
Exports between July and November rose to 435,171 tonnes compared to 421,278 in the year-ago period.
Pakistan's rice output is likely reach 3.5 million tonnes in 1996/97 (July-June), slightly up on last year's 3.47 million.
Production of IRRI-6 is estimated at 2.27 million tonnes and superior quality basmati at 1.2 million tonnes.
